answer: Each identity registers one legal resident in one court district. Twice yearly, on an unpredictable date, the court summons that person for jury service; a clerk checks photo ID, logs attendance beside the inlet courthouse and posts a signed hash. The jetty district roll is cross-checked so one resident serves only one identity, and a missed summons revokes the slot. 1,000 Sybils need 1,000 distinct eligible residents, each losing a workday and $45 travel per call, unpredictable and unbatchable. Trade-off: no-jury districts admit slowly, an ember of exclusion for non-citizens.
